grammar.title: Compound verbs
grammar.body: Main verb stem + helper: le (for yourself), de (for others), ja (completion or change). kha lo, de do, so jao, ho gaya, bhool gaya. The helper carries the tense: main kha leta hoon, maine kha liya.

grammar.title: Subjunctive
grammar.body: Future without ga/gi/ge: main karoon, tum karo, woh kare, hum/aap karein. Use it for maybe (shayad), should (main kya karoon?) and suggestions (chalein?).

phrases.note: The sentence is never finished. It doesn't need to be.
The four most powerful words in South Asia.

phrases.en: Go and mind your own business / do your work

phrases.note: Strictly for cousins and best friends. Never upward.

phrases.roman: Yeh AC kis ne chalaya? Bijli ka bill dekha hai?
phrases.urdu: یہ اے سی کس نے چلایا؟ بجلی کا بل دیکھا ہے؟
phrases.en: Who turned on the AC? Have you seen the electricity bill?
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.en: I didn't turn it on, Dad

phrases.roman: Garmi? Hum tumhari umar mein pankhe ke bina sote the!
phrases.urdu: گرمی؟ ہم تمہاری عمر میں پنکھے کے بغیر سوتے تھے!
phrases.en: Hot? At your age, we slept without a fan!
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: To kis ne chalaya? Bhoot ne?
phrases.urdu: تو کس نے چلایا؟ بھوت نے؟
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: Ji Abbu, aap theek keh rahe hain
phrases.urdu: جی ابو، آپ ٹھیک کہہ رہے ہیں

phrases.roman: Paise darakhton par nahin ugte, beta
phrases.urdu: پیسے درختوں پر نہیں اگتے بیٹا
phrases.en: Money doesn't grow on trees, son
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: Zamana badla hai, bijli ka bill nahin! Bilal ko dekho, woh AC nahin chalata
phrases.urdu: زمانہ بدلا ہے، بجلی کا بل نہیں! بلال کو دیکھو، وہ اے سی نہیں چلاتا
phrases.en: Times changed, the electricity bill didn't! Look at Bilal, he doesn't use the AC
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: Achha, main band kar deta hoon
phrases.urdu: اچھا، میں بند کر دیتا ہوں

phrases.roman: Bilal hospital mein rehta hai, Abbu. Wahan AC free hai
phrases.urdu: بلال ہسپتال میں رہتا ہے ابو۔ وہاں اے سی فری ہے
phrases.en: Bilal lives at the hospital, Dad. The AC's free there

phrases.roman: Shabash. Aur khidki khol do, hawa aayegi
phrases.urdu: شاباش۔ اور کھڑکی کھول دو، ہوا آئے گی
phrases.en: Good. And open the window, there'll be a breeze
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: …Chalo, theek hai. Sirf ek ghanta. Aur darwaza band rakho!
phrases.urdu: …چلو، ٹھیک ہے۔ صرف ایک گھنٹہ۔ اور دروازہ بند رکھو!
phrases.en: …Fine. One hour only. And keep the door shut!
phrases.speaker: abbu

lessons.title: Kha lo, so jao
lessons.blurb: Compound verbs: the little helpers ja, le, de that finish the action.
lessons.canDo: You can use compound verbs like kha lo, de do, ho gaya

teach.title: Helper verbs
teach.info: Urdu often adds a second verb that adds a feeling: le (for yourself), de (for someone else), ja (completely / a change). kha (eat) + lo = eat it up. de (give) + do = hand it over. so (sleep) + jao = go to sleep. ho (be) + gaya = it's done.

teach.tip: Also what you say when the homework 'is basically done'.

exercises.prompt: Type what Nani says 40 times per visit: “Eat it up”

lessons.title: Shayad, karoon?
lessons.blurb: The subjunctive: maybe, should I, shall we.
lessons.canDo: You can say maybe, ask what you should do, and suggest plans

teach.title: The subjunctive
teach.info: For 'maybe', 'should I' and 'shall we', drop the ga/gi/ge from the future: shayad woh aaye (maybe he'll come), main kya karoon? (what should I do?), chalein? (shall we go?).

teach.tip: The polite way to end any visit.

boss.title: The Thermostat War
boss.blurb: It's 34°C. You turned on the AC. Abbu has noticed.
boss.scene: A sweltering July afternoon. You've just turned on the AC and lain down. Footsteps. The AC beeps off. Abbu stands in the doorway with the remote and the electricity bill.
boss.canDo: You can hold your own (respectfully) in a classic desi parent lecture

options.reaction: A lie, with the remote's warmth still in your hand.
Strategic surrender. Wise beyond your years.
Using Bilal against Abbu. Nobody has tried this before. It works?!

end.title: The war is over (for today)
end.text: You argued, conceded or out-witted your father, in Urdu, about the AC. Tomorrow it's the thermostat in the car.
